messages.claude:
fix: track script classes via _script_classes registry instead of __torch_script_class__ attribute

Replace the `__torch_script_class__` attribute marker on classes with
lookups against the `_script_classes` registry in `_state.py`. The
attribute-based check was unreliable for inheritance detection in
implicit scripting codepaths (e.g. `try_ann_to_type`), where a
subclass could be mistaken for (or fail to be recognized as) an
already-compiled script class because the marker only lived on the
class that was directly compiled, not on subclasses resolved through
the annotation path.

Why: `try_ann_to_type` used `hasattr(ann, "__torch_script_class__")`
to decide whether a class was already compiled. This short-circuited
inheritance resolution for classes encountered through implicit
scripting: a subclass referenced in an annotation would not carry the
attribute, so the registry lookup failed and the class was either
re-compiled or misclassified. Switching to `_get_script_class` (keyed
by qualified name) gives a single source of truth and correctly
identifies previously compiled classes regardless of how they are
reached.

Changes:
- Remove `cls.__torch_script_class__ = True` assignment in
  `_add_script_class`; rely solely on `_script_classes[name]`.
- Update `try_ann_to_type` to resolve the qualified name once and
  check `_get_script_class(qualified_name)` for both enum and class
  branches, reusing the resolved name for the returned `ClassType`.
- Clear `torch.jit._state._script_classes` in `clear_class_registry`
  so tests start from a clean registry.
- Add `test_class_inheritance_implicit` covering the implicit
  scripting inheritance path via `try_ann_to_type`.
messages.minimax:
fix: detect script class inheritance via registry lookup instead of attribute marker

The `__torch_script_class__` attribute marker was removed and replaced with a registry-based lookup using `_get_script_class(qualified_name)`. This ensures class inheritance is correctly detected in implicit scripting codepaths like `try_ann_to_type`, and avoids relying on a side-effect attribute that could produce false positives. Added a test to verify implicit inheritance detection raises appropriate errors when accessing nonexistent attributes.
messages.kimi:
fix: Fix class inheritance detection in implicit JIT scripting codepaths

This PR fixes a bug where class inheritance was not properly detected in implicit scripting codepaths (e.g., `try_ann_to_type`). The issue occurred because `_add_script_class` was setting a `__torch_script_class__` attribute on classes, but this attribute was not being properly checked in all codepaths, leading to incorrect behavior when dealing with inherited classes.

The fix removes the `__torch_script_class__` attribute assignment and instead uses the `_get_script_class` registry consistently to check if a class has been scripted. This ensures that inheritance relationships are properly respected across all JIT scripting codepaths.

Changes:
- Remove `cls.__torch_script_class__ = True` from `_add_script_class` in `torch/jit/_state.py`
- Update `try_ann_to_type` in `torch/jit/annotations.py` to use `_get_script_class` instead of `hasattr(ann, "__torch_script_class__")`
- Add test case `test_class_inheritance_implicit` to verify the fix
- Update `clear_class_registry` to also clear `_script_classes` registry

This is a follow-up on the previous dtensor redistribute PR: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/150740, which enables SimpleFSDP's mixed-precision training.

In the most recent integration in TorchTitan: https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/1250, we found some discrepancies between SimpleFSDP's `fully_shard` and `replicate` modes when MPT is enabled. This PR fixes this issue and corrects previously added test cases.

The previous code used `unittest.main()` as the test entry point, which
prevents tests from being properly registered with PyTorch's distributed
test harness. This caused the test cases to not be discovered/run through
the standard `torch.testing._internal.common_utils.run_tests()` runner,

and parameterization for these tests.

Switch to `run_tests()` so the tests are correctly registered and
executed within the expected test infrastructure.

messages.kimi:
feat: [ONNX] Add support for nested tuple and dict outputs in shape type inference

Refactor ONNXAssignOutputShape to use recursive function that handles arbitrarily nested tuples, lists, and dictionaries in model outputs. The previous implementation only supported one level of nesting and failed to correctly handle complex nested structures like tuples containing other tuples or dictionaries with tuple values.

This change unrolls nested structures recursively, ensuring proper shape and type propagation through all output hierarchy levels. Added comprehensive test cases for dict outputs, tuple outputs, and nested tuple outputs to verify the fix.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] Support nested tuple and dict outputs in shape type inference

Refactors ONNXAssignOutputShape into a recursive helper that walks the
output Python object tree and assigns shape/type info to flattened graph
outputs. The previous iterative implementation only handled one level of
nesting, so models returning nested tuples (e.g. (a, ((b,), (c, d)))) or
dict outputs (e.g. OrderedDict subclass with tensor/tuple/list fields)
hit assertions or produced incorrect output types during export.

The recursive version uniformly handles tensors, tuples, lists, dicts
(unrolled to fixed-size key/value pairs per ONNX constraints), and
strings (ignored). Each branch advances a shared outputs_index and
bounds-checks it against graph->outputs().size().

Adds three tests covering dict output (OrderedDict subclass), flat
tuple output, and nested tuple output via test_pytorch_onnx_onnxruntime
to guard against regressions.
messages.minimax:
[ONNX] Refactor ONNXAssignOutputShape to use recursion for nested outputs

Refactor ONNXAssignOutputShape to handle complex nested output structures (tuples, lists, dicts) recursively instead of iteratively. The new recursive implementation processes each output element individually, properly tracking the output index through nested structures. This improves code maintainability by eliminating the repetitive for-loop with duplicated index tracking logic, and correctly handles arbitrary nesting depth of tuples and lists.

messages.kimi:
Based on the code changes, I can see this is fixing a bug in the ONNX symbolic opset11 where `index_put` fails when the `values` parameter is a scalar (rank 0 tensor). The fix adds a check to expand scalar values before reshaping.

fix: Handle scalar values in ONNX index_put symbolic function

The `index_put` symbolic function in opset11 fails when the `values` parameter is a scalar (0-dimensional tensor) because it attempts to reshape the scalar without first expanding it to match the broadcast shape. This causes shape mismatch errors during ONNX export when using scalar assignments like `mask[indices] = True` or `mask[indices] = 5.5`.

Add a rank check for the values tensor and expand scalar values to the expected shape before reshaping. This ensures proper handling of singular value assignments in index_put operations.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] Fix index_put with singular values

When `index_put` is called with a singular (0-rank) value tensor (e.g., a scalar Python value converted to tensor like `torch.tensor(5.5)` or a Python scalar), the ONNX exporter would directly reshape the values to `values_shape`. This fails because Reshape requires the element count to match, but a scalar tensor cannot be reshaped to a non-singleton shape without first being broadcast.

Detect the singular case via `_get_tensor_rank(values)` and expand the scalar to `values_shape` before the Reshape op, so the subsequent reshape is valid. Added test coverage for both bool and float masks with scalar index_put to prevent regressions.
messages.minimax:
[ONNX] Fix index_put with singular (scalar) values (#152345)

The index_put symbolic function did not handle scalar values correctly during ONNX export. When assigning a singular value like `mask[indices] = True` or `mask[indices] = torch.tensor(5.5)`, the reshape operation would fail because scalar values lack the required shape information.

This change adds a rank check in symbolic_opset11.index_put: if values is a scalar (rank 0), it is expanded to the appropriate shape before reshaping, matching how the operation behaves in PyTorch eager mode. Tests are added for both boolean and float scalar assignments.

messages.kimi:
Looking at the code changes, I need to analyze what changed and why.

What changed:
In both `pixel_shuffle` and `pixel_unshuffle` functions, the `std::iota` call was changed from using `-added_dims_shape.size()` as the starting value to using `0`.

Why this matters:
The change fixes the permutation logic for batch dimensions. The original code used negative indices which could cause incorrect behavior when calculating the permutation for reshaping operations. By starting from `0` instead of a negative offset, the batch dimensions are correctly indexed.

This appears to be a bug fix where the negative offset calculation was incorrect, causing potential issues with the pixel shuffle/unshuffle operations when handling batch dimensions.

Based on the reference examples and the nature of this change (fixing incorrect indexing logic), here's the commit message:

fix: correct batch dimension indexing in pixel_shuffle and pixel_unshuffle

The std::iota call was using negative offset (-added_dims_shape.size()) to compute batch dimension indices, which caused incorrect permutation calculations. Changed to start from 0 to properly maintain batch dims in the permutation vector, ensuring correct tensor reshaping behavior for pixel shuffle operations.
messages.claude:
fix: use positive offsets for batch dims in pixel_shuffle/unshuffle permutation

The batch dimension offsets in the permutation were computed using negative
indices starting from -added_dims_shape.size(), which relied on the assumption
that exactly 2 dims were added to the reshaped tensor. This coupling made the
permutation logic fragile and hard to reason about.

Use std::iota starting from 0 instead, since the batch dims are the leading
dims of the reshaped tensor and the negative offsets for the trailing
(oc/h/w and upscale/downscale_factor) dims are unaffected by this change.
The behavior is unchanged but the intent is now explicit and correct.
messages.minimax:
Fix incorrect batch dimension offsets in pixel_shuffle and pixel_unshuffle

The batch dimension offsets in std::iota were using -added_dims_shape.size() which produced incorrect permutation indices. Changed to use 0 for correct batch dimension handling.

Reland fast gather and index implementation (#151917)

This PR reapplies #151490 and #151753 together, and adds some missing checks when applying the fast path.
Previously missed checks:
1) indexing path has the stride in the indexed dimension in bytes, gather path has the stride in the indexed dimension in elements. When checking if fast path is applicable, I didn't take this difference into account, and still multiplied the indexing stride by element size. Fixed and test added
2) We want to take fast path only when we are copying contiguous equally spaced slices of inputs + all the necessary alignment requirements. The effective tensor size should be 2d (after all possible flattening is applied), the index stride in the last dimension should be 0, and, since in the kernel we are not applying non-indexing-related offsets to src tensor, the src tensor stride in the second dimension should be 0. This automatically happens for gather with dim=0, so I didn't put in an explicit condition for this. Sometimes all conditions except first dim "effective" stride equal to 0 are satisfied for scatter on non-zero dim, when index size in the indexing dimension is 1 and thus it is collapsed (dimensions of size 1 are always collapsed), e.g.
```
        # test gather along 1st dim that can accidentally trigger fast path
        # because due to index dimension in the gather dim being 1
        # an unexpected squashing in tensorIterator happens
        src = make_tensor((16, 2, 16), device=device, dtype=dtype)
        ind = torch.randint(2, (16, 1), device=device).view(16, 1, 1).expand(16, 1, 16)
        res = torch.gather(src, dim=1, index=ind)
        if res.device.type == "cuda":
            ref_cpu = torch.gather(src.cpu(), dim=1, index=ind.cpu())
            self.assertEqual(res.cpu(), ref_cpu, atol=0, rtol=0)
```
Note that if index size here was (16, 2, 16) instead of (16, 1, 16) then the middle dimension could not be collapsed and we wouldn't end up incorrectly taking fast path.
We could update the kernel to take this stride into account when computing offsets into src tensor, or we could specifically disallow non-zero stride on the first dimension. I took the second path for now.

Use cub::DeviceRadixSort instead of thrust for randperm_out_cuda

Replace thrust-based sorting with CUB's DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs in randperm_out_cuda to improve performance. The change also adds a TORCH_CHECK to ensure n does not exceed INT_MAX, and uses the CUDACachingAllocator for proper temporary storage management.
messages.kimi:
Looking at the code changes, I can see this is a refactoring of the `randperm_out_cuda` function in PyTorch's CUDA tensor factories. The key changes are:

1. Replacing thrust-based sorting with CUB's `DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs`
2. Adding a check for `n <= INT_MAX` 
3. Using raw pointers instead of `thrust::device_ptr`
4. Removing the THCThrustAllocator dependency

This is a performance improvement (CUB is typically faster than thrust) and also a refactor (cleaner code, removing deprecated THC dependencies).

Based on the reference examples and the nature of the changes, here's the commit message:

perf: replace thrust with CUB radix sort in randperm_out_cuda

Replace thrust::sort_by_key with cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs for improved performance on CUDA. The CUB implementation provides better performance characteristics for the random permutation operation by using optimized radix sort algorithms.

Additionally:
- Add TORCH_CHECK for INT_MAX limit to prevent overflow issues
- Remove THCThrustAllocator dependency (part of ongoing THC cleanup)
- Use raw pointers instead of thrust::device_ptr for cleaner code
- Add <cub/cub.cuh> and <limits> headers as required

This change aligns with the broader effort to modernize CUDA implementations and remove deprecated THC code paths.
messages.claude:
performance: replace thrust sort with cub::DeviceRadixSort in randperm_out_cuda

Replace the thrust-based sort_by_key path in `randperm_out_cuda` with
`cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs`. The previous implementation relied on
thrust's CUDA policy and the custom `THCThrustAllocator`, which funnels
allocations through `globalContext().getTHCState()` — a legacy THC-era
dependency that is being phased out. CUB's device-radix sort is also
noticeably faster than thrust's generic sort_by_key for the
integer-keyed permutation case (single-pass radix over sizeof(scalar_t)*8
bits), and it integrates directly with `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator`
for temporary storage instead of going through the thrust allocator
shim.

Additional changes motivated by the rewrite:
- Add a `TORCH_CHECK` guarding `n <= INT_MAX`, since CUB's APIs index
  elements with `int` and silently overflow for larger permutations.
- Drop the explicit `thrust::sequence` fill of the values array and
  instead sort a pre-built `at::arange(n)` range tensor as the values,
  which avoids a separate kernel launch.
- Use raw `scalar_t*` pointers instead of `thrust::device_ptr` wrappers,
  removing the thrust dependency from this translation unit entirely.

Make torch._chunk_cat support non-contiguous inputs (#151263)

Currently, `torch._chunk_cat` only supports contiguous inputs (due to `.view()` usage in `_pad_chunk()` supporting only contiguous tensor). This doesn't work for internal models where there can be non-contiguous input tensors:

- size=[8192, 16416], stride=[16448, 1]  # stride[0] is larger than size[1]
- size=[1152, 384], stride=[1, 1152]  # column-major tensor

In this PR, we relax the assumption on contiguous input tensor, by switching from `.view()` to `.reshape()`. Note that since `.reshape()` will try to use `.view()` under the hood whenever possible, this should not cause regression to existing use cases.

messages.kimi:
refactor: Move detach implementation to TensorShape.cpp and use native::alias

Moves the detach() function from TensorProperties.cpp to TensorShape.cpp
to improve code organization by colocating it with related tensor
operations like alias(). Also updates the implementation to use
native::alias(self) instead of simply returning self, ensuring proper
tensor aliasing behavior.
messages.claude:
refactor: move detach() from TensorProperties to TensorShape and alias the input tensor

The `detach()` implementation previously lived in `TensorProperties.cpp` and
returned `self` unchanged, meaning the returned tensor shared storage and
autograd history with the input. This made `detach` a no-op rather than a true
detach, so callers could not rely on it to break the autograd link.

`detach` is relocated to `TensorShape.cpp` (alongside `alias`) and now returns
`native::alias(self)`. Aliasing produces a tensor that views the same data but
exposes a fresh autograd node entry point, which is the hook that `VariableType`
and `Declarations.yaml` rely on to detach the tensor from the autograd graph.
This fixes the underlying bug where `detach` silently failed to detach.
messages.minimax:
refactor: move detach from TensorProperties to TensorShape with proper aliasing

The detach() function was a no-op stub in TensorProperties that simply returned
the input tensor unchanged. Move it to TensorShape and implement it to call
native::alias(self), which properly creates an alias of the tensor rather than
returning self. This provides the correct hook behavior for VariableType and
ensures detach creates a proper tensor alias as expected.

messages.claude:
fix(onnx): support dynamic repeats in repeat_interleave opset13 export

Move the repeat_interleave symbolic implementation from opset11 to opset13 and rework it to support dynamic repeats tensors. The opset11 version only handled the case where repeats was a single value or a 1-d tensor with known static size along a dynamic input dim; it delegated everything else to the opset9 fallback, which raised "Unsupported for cases with dynamic repeats" whenever repeats_sizes[0] was None. This blocked ONNX export of models that pass a dynamically-shaped repeats vector to torch.repeat_interleave (e.g. repeats coming from another op's output).

The new opset13 implementation:
- Adds a cond_dynamic_repeats branch that, when repeats is a dynamic 1-d tensor, emits a Where node to either expand a scalar repeat or keep the original tensor, instead of unconditionally falling through to opset9.
- Replaces the Transpose+Reshape post-processing of the Loop scan output with a SequenceEmpty/SequenceInsert accumulator inside the loop followed by ConcatFromSequence along dim, which correctly handles the dynamic-repeat case where the per-iteration split sizes are not known at export time.
- Bumps the min opset for unsupported dynamic-repeat cases in opset9 from 11 to 13, and updates the test's skipIfUnsupportedMinOpsetVersion from 11 to 13 accordingly.

Test changes expand test_dynamic_repeat_interleave to cover float inputs and dynamic repeats (both scalar and multi-element), and add test_multiple_dynamic_repeat_interleave to exercise 1-d repeats vectors with multiple dynamic values along both dim=0 and dim=1.
messages.kimi:
[ONNX] Support dynamic repeats in repeat_interleave for opset 13

Moves repeat_interleave implementation from opset 11 to opset 13 to enable
support for dynamic repeats tensors. The previous implementation used
Transpose + Reshape which couldn't handle cases where the repeats tensor
has unknown dimensions. The new implementation uses ConcatFromSequence
(available in opset 13) to properly concatenate loop outputs along the
specified dimension, enabling export of repeat_interleave with dynamic
repeats.

Also updates test cases to reflect the new minimum opset version and adds
tests for multiple dynamic repeats scenarios.
messages.minimax:
[ONNX] Move repeat_interleave to opset13 with dynamic repeats support

Move repeat_interleave from opset11 to opset13 to support dynamic repeats.
The opset11 implementation only handled static/repeats-dim-known cases, and
fell back to opset9 for dynamic scenarios which lacked proper support. The new
implementation in opset13 properly handles dynamic repeats using a where node
to substitute for conditionals, sequence operations for collecting outputs,
and ConcatFromSequence for the final result. Also add new test cases covering
multiple dynamic repeat scenarios including different dimensions and input
combinations.

messages.claude:
feat: support F16 dtype by reusing c10::Half instead of stubbed half struct

What
- Replace the unimplemented `lazy_tensors::half` stub struct (which only logged
  `FATAL`) with a `using half = c10::Half;` alias in `types.h`, pulling in
  `<c10/util/Half.h>`.
- Add a `PrimitiveType::F16 -> at::ScalarType::Half` mapping in
  `shape_util.h::PrimitiveToScalarType` so F16 shapes convert correctly.
- Drop the now-redundant `Caster<at::Half>` and `NeedCast<at::Half>`
  specializations in `tensor_util.cpp` (the `lazy_tensors::half` alias path
  handles casting).
- Add `TestAddHalf` and `TestAddMixedPrecision` tests covering half-precision
  and mixed float/half addition.

Why
The previous `lazy_tensors::half` type was a placeholder that crashed on any
operation (every method/operator emitted `LTC_LOG(FATAL) << "Not implemented
yet."`). This blocked any F16 tensor from flowing through LazyTensorCore
because the type could not be constructed, converted, or operated on. By
aliasing to PyTorch's fully-implemented `c10::Half`, LTC inherits correct
half-precision semantics (storage, conversion, arithmetic) for free, and
registering the `F16` primitive in `PrimitiveToScalarType` ensures that
half tensors round-trip through LTC's shape system instead of falling through
to an unmapped case. The removed `Caster`/`NeedCast` specializations for
`at::Half` were a workaround for the old stub and are superseded by the alias.
The new tests verify that half and mixed-precision addition now execute
correctly on LTC devices.
messages.minimax:
feat: enable half-precision float (FP16) support via c10::Half

The `lazy_tensors::half` type was a stub that would FATAL on any operation, making FP16 unusable. This change replaces it with `c10::Half` which provides a working implementation. Added `NeedCast`/`Caster` support for `lazy_tensors::half` (not `at::Half`), and proper F16→Half scalar type mapping in shape_util. Added tests for half-precision addition and mixed-precision (float+half) addition.
messages.kimi:
feat: Add FP16 (half precision) support for lazy tensor operations

Replace the stub `lazy_tensors::half` implementation with `c10::Half` to enable proper FP16 support in lazy tensor core. This change removes the placeholder half type that only logged fatal errors and replaces it with PyTorch's native half precision type.

The changes include:
- Replace custom `lazy_tensors::half` struct with `using half = c10::Half` alias
- Remove redundant `Caster<at::Half>` and `NeedCast<at::Half>` specializations since `lazy_tensors::half` now maps to `c10::Half`
- Add F16 to ScalarType conversion in `PrimitiveToScalarType`
- Add test cases for half precision tensor operations (`TestAddHalf`) and mixed precision operations (`TestAddMixedPrecision`)

This enables users to perform arithmetic operations on FP16 tensors through the lazy tensor backend, which is essential for memory-efficient training and inference on hardware with native FP16 support.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add ONNX symbolic support for torch.log10

Adds a symbolic function for `torch.log10` in ONNX opset 9 by implementing it as `log(x) / ln(10)`. This enables users to export PyTorch models using the log10 operation to ONNX format. The implementation uses the mathematical identity log10(x) = ln(x) / ln(10) since ONNX does not have a native Log10 operator. Includes a test case to verify correct export and runtime behavior with ONNX Runtime.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] Add symbolic converter for torch.log10

Add a symbolic_opset9 converter that decomposes torch.log10 into the
natural log of the input divided by ln(10) (2.30258509299404568401),
produced via ONNX Div and Constant ops. ONNX has no native Log10 op, so
expressing it in terms of Log + Div keeps the exported graph numerically
correct and consistent with how log1p is already lowered in the same
file.

Add a corresponding ort test (test_log10) to verify the exported model
runs against onnxruntime, matching the pattern used by neighboring
unary math ops such as test_log1p.

Why:
- ONNX does not define a Log10 operator, so torch.log10 could not be
  exported directly. Decomposing as log(x) / ln(10) is the standard
  lowering and aligns with the existing log1p implementation.
- The constant uses the full-precision ln(10) value to minimize
  numerical drift versus the eager PyTorch result.
- The test guards against future regressions by exercising the new
  converter end-to-end through onnxruntime.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add nll_loss_forward operator support to Lazy Tensor Core

Implement the nll_loss_forward operator in the Lazy Tensor Core backend to support PyTorch's aten::nll_loss_forward operation. This change renames the existing NllLoss class to NllLossForward, updates it to return two outputs (loss and total_weight) instead of one, and adds the corresponding lowering logic in the TS backend. The implementation aligns with PyTorch's native nll_loss_forward semantics which returns both the computed loss and the total weight used in the reduction, enabling proper gradient computation in autograd.
messages.minimax:
feat: add nll_loss_forward native function support

Add nll_loss_forward as a first-class lazy tensor native function to properly support PyTorch's autograd mechanism. The existing nll_loss implementation returned only the loss tensor (num_outputs=1), but PyTorch's nll_loss_forward returns a tuple of (loss, total_weight) needed for correct backward pass computation. This change renames the IR node from NllLoss to NllLossForward, updates num_outputs to 2, and adds the corresponding lowering and native function wiring to enable proper forward/backward semantics.
messages.claude:
feat: rename nll_loss to nll_loss_forward and add total_weight output

Rename the NllLoss op to NllLossForward and align it with the
at::aten::nll_loss_forward ATen op so that the lazy backend returns
both the loss and the total_weight tensor. The previous NllLoss only
produced a single output (the loss), which meant the corresponding
backward pass had no access to the total_weight computed during the
forward pass and could not match the semantics of the eager
nll_loss_forward/backward pair.

Why:
- The eager aten::nll_loss_forward op returns a tuple (output,
  total_weight), and nll_loss_backward consumes total_weight as an
  input. The lazy tensor core implementation only modeled the loss
  output, so backward had to be lowered separately and could not reuse
  the total_weight from the forward node, leading to incorrect or
  divergent behavior between lazy and eager paths.
- By switching to at::aten::nll_loss_forward and setting num_outputs=2
  on the node, the forward op now produces both outputs. The new
  InferNllLossForward lowering derives the tuple shape (loss + scalar
  total_weight), and LowerNllLossForward lowers it via LowerBuiltin so
  the TS backend invokes the real aten op.
- Registering nll_loss_forward in ts_native_functions.yaml and adding
  LazyNativeFunctions::nll_loss_forward bridges the eager-to-lazy
  dispatch so calls on Lazy tensors route through the new forward node.
- The backward lowering was also reordered so nll_loss_backward is
  handled alongside the new forward lowering, keeping both sides of the
  loss consistent.

messages.kimi:
Based on the code changes, I can see this is a bug fix in the ONNX constant folding pass. The change modifies the `squeeze()` call to include the `axis` parameter, which fixes incorrect behavior when gathering with scalar indices.

fix: Correct Gather constant folding with scalar indices

The Gather operation constant folding was incorrectly squeezing all dimensions when handling scalar indices, instead of only squeezing the specified axis dimension. This caused shape mismatches when the input tensor had other singleton dimensions that should be preserved.

The fix passes the `axis` parameter to `squeeze()` to ensure only the intended dimension is removed, maintaining correct tensor shapes for downstream operations.
messages.claude:
fix: squeeze specific axis in ONNX Gather constant fold

The previous constant fold for ONNX Gather called squeeze() with no
arguments, which removes all size-1 dimensions. When the input tensor
had multiple size-1 dimensions (e.g. a buffer shaped [1, 1, 3, 1, 1]),
this collapsed more axes than the Gather op semantically should, producing
an incorrect folded constant and a wrong output rank/shape downstream.

Pass the actual `axis` to squeeze so only the indexed dimension is
removed, matching Gather's output rank rule (rank_of_input - 1 when the
index is a scalar).

A new test case is added covering a Gather on a 5D constant buffer with
multiple singleton dims, using dynamic axes, to guard against regression.
The min opset 11 skip on test_gather_constant_fold is also removed since
the fold now behaves correctly at lower opsets.
messages.minimax:
[ONNX] Fix squeeze axis in constant fold for gather ops

The squeeze() call was missing the axis parameter, causing it to remove all
dimensions of size 1 instead of only the specific axis. This resulted in
incorrect constant folding for gather operations.

Also adds a new test case for GatherModule with registered buffers and
dynamic axes to cover the previously skipped scenario.

feat: add zero_ in-place op for lazy tensor backend

Registers the zero_ in-place operator with the LTS TS backend by adding the
native function binding in ts_native_functions.yaml and implementing
LazyNativeFunctions::zero_ in aten_ltc_ts_type.cpp, which delegates to
LazyTensor::zero_ via the existing bridge.

Previously zero_ fell back to the default Aten implementation, which on the
lazy path materialized an eager fill or fell back through the dispatcher,
bypassing the lazy IR and defeating graph capture for in-place zeroing. This
caused incorrect/incomplete graphs (and unexpected synchronizations) for any
model that calls torch.zero_ on a lazy tensor (e.g. gradient zeroing, weight
init). Adding an explicit lazy lowering ensures zero_ is recorded as a lazy
node so it composes with the rest of the captured graph.

Also adds TestZeroInPlace to verify the lazy output matches the eager output
across devices.

Register `threshold_backward` in the lazy tensor core TS backend so that gradient computation for `torch.threshold` flows through the LTC graph instead of falling back to the eager Aten implementation.

Why:

feat: support default in-place random_ in LTC TS backend

Replace the old DiscreteUniform op (which required explicit from/to bounds
and a manual RNG seed) with a simpler Random op that delegates to the
aten::random_ builtin. The previous implementation forced users to pass a
[from, to) range, but the aten::random API only has in-place variants and
does not expose from/to parameters — so the LTC lowering was producing a
node the TS backend could not map onto the real aten semantics.

The new Random node uses the QualString "aten::random_" symbol directly
since aten::random is not registered as a recognizable builtin function.
Add a LazyNativeFunctions::random_ dispatch entry that falls back to the
eager implementation when a user-provided generator is set, and register
random_ in ts_native_functions.yaml so it reaches the TS lowering path.
Update LazyTensor::random_ to drop the from/to/seed arguments and add a
test covering the default (no-arg) in-place case across dtypes.
messages.kimi:
Looking at this diff, I need to understand what changed:

1. What changed:
   - Deleted `discrete_uniform.cpp` and renamed `discrete_uniform.h` to `random.h`
   - Created new `random.cpp` with a simpler `Random` class
   - The `Random` class now only takes a single `input` parameter instead of `from`, `to`, and `seed`
   - Updated `LazyTensor::random_()` to use the new simpler `Random` op
   - Added `random_` to the supported native functions list
   - Added a new test `TestRandomInPlaceDefault`

2. Why:
   - The old `DiscreteUniform` was overly complex for the `random_` operation
   - The new implementation simplifies the random operation by removing the `from`/`to` range parameters
   - This aligns with PyTorch's `random_()` which doesn't require explicit range bounds
   - The comment in the code explains: "aten::random builtin symbol cannot be recognized as a builtin function since random only has in-place versions. Therefore we force the symbol to be 'aten::random_' here."

3. Commit type: This is a `refactor` - restructuring the code to simplify the random operation implementation without changing the core behavior (though the API signature changes to be simpler).

Based on the reference examples showing patterns like "[BE]" (best effort) and descriptive messages explaining both what and why:


refactor: Simplify random_ implementation by replacing DiscreteUniform with Random op

The DiscreteUniform class was overly complex for the random_ operation, requiring
from/to range parameters and seed management. Replace it with a simpler Random
op that only takes the input tensor, aligning with PyTorch's random_() API which
doesn't require explicit range bounds.

Since aten::random only has in-place versions and cannot be recognized as a
builtin function, we explicitly use "aten::random_" as the operation symbol.

Also add random_ to the supported native functions list and include a test for
the default random_ behavior across all tensor dtypes.

aten::random_ symbol. The old DiscreteUniform used aten::random which is not

implementation correctly uses aten::random_ to align with PyTorch's standard
in-place random_ semantics, which generates values in [0, 2^64) for integer
dtypes or [0, 1) for float dtypes. The API is also simplified to match PyTorch's

Add env for disabling meta reference on functionalization. (#148822)

Fix: https://github.com/pytorch/xla/issues/8755

This PR introduces `TORCH_DISABLE_FUNCTIONALIZATION_META_REFERENCE`
environment variable. Setting this variable makes it so the
functionalization kernels won't run the meta reference, which is used to
propagate expected sizes and strides.

Currently, PyTorch/XLA doesn't actually propagates the correct strides
to its tensors. It was also shown that calling these meta functions may
incur in significant overhead.

Running the provided minimal reproducer (see issue), we see a speedup
close to 4.3x:

- Baseline: 0.0747s
- `XLA_DISABLE_FUNCTIONALIZATION=1`: 0.0159s
- `TORCH_DISABLE_FUNCTIONALIZATION_META_REFERENCE=1`: 0.0175s

In summary, this PR:

- Creates the `disable_meta_reference()` function, which checks whether
  the environment variable is set
- Modifies codegen for functionalization kernels, adding the call to
  `disable_meta_reference()` function to the appropriate conditions
- Creates a new bash function for running `lazy/test_ts_opinfo.py` with
  the environment variable set

1. Code Changes Analysis:
   - In `torch/fx/graph.py`: The code modifies how `getattr` is handled in the FX graph codegen. It adds a check for `len(node.args) == 2` to ensure that only 2-argument `getattr` calls are treated as attribute access (pretty-printed), while 3-argument `getattr` calls (with default value) fall through to be treated as regular function calls.
   - In `test/test_fx.py`: A new test `test_torch_fx_getattr` is added to verify that 3-argument `getattr` with a default value works correctly.

2. The Issue Being Fixed:
   Before this fix, 3-argument `getattr(obj, attr, default)` calls would incorrectly match the condition for pretty-printing attribute access because the code only checked if the second argument was a valid identifier. This caused the default value argument to be lost in the generated code.

3. Commit Type:
   This is a fix - it fixes a bug where 3-argument `getattr` wasn't being handled correctly in FX graph codegen.

fix: Handle 3-argument getattr in FX graph codegen

Fixes a bug where `getattr(x, 'attr', default)` with a default value was incorrectly treated as attribute access instead of a function call. The codegen was only checking if the second argument was a valid identifier, causing the default value to be lost in the generated code.

Added a length check to ensure only 2-argument getattr calls (attribute access) are pretty-printed, while 3-argument calls fall through to be handled as regular function calls with all arguments preserved.
messages.minimax:
fix (torch.fx): handle 3-argument getattr correctly in graph codegen

Previously, the pretty-print logic for `getattr` in `emit_node` only checked that the second argument was a string identifier, but didn't distinguish between 2-argument (attribute access) and 3-argument (with default value) forms. This caused 3-argument `getattr(x, 'nonexistent_attr', torch.Tensor([2, 3]))` to be incorrectly pretty-printed as attribute access, producing invalid Python code. The fix adds a `len(node.args) == 2` check to ensure only the 2-argument form gets the pretty-print treatment.

messages.claude:
[ONNX] Fix integer floor division and remainder export for opset 7/8, refine true_divide type handling

Refactors the ONNX symbolic ops to correctly support integer floor division and remainder across opset versions:

- Remove the opset7 `div`/`_div_rounding_mode`/`_floor_divide` implementations that raised a RuntimeError for integer inputs and relied on `Floor(Div)` for floats. Integer floor division now falls through to opset9's `_floor_divide`, which uses `Mod`/`Where` to match PyTorch semantics for negative operands.
- Rewrite opset9 `_floor_divide`'s fixup step to use `Mul(fixup_mask, 1)` + `Sub` instead of selecting between `div-1` and `div`, and route `Less` through the new `_lt_helper` so opset<=8 exports use the opset8 `lt` implementation. This fixes incorrect results for negative integer floor division.
- Simplify `true_divide` to rely on implicit casting in the scalar type analysis pass when either input is floating, instead of emitting explicit `Cast` nodes for each branch.
- Add opset11 `remainder` that emits ONNX `Mod` (fmod=0) for integer inputs and delegates to opset9 for floating point; update opset9 `remainder` to reuse `_floor_divide` so negative operands round toward negative infinity rather than toward zero.
- Drop the now-unnecessary opset7 re-export of `div` from opset8.

Tests:
- Switch `FloorDivModule` inputs from `randn` to `arange(-2, 4)` so negative values are exercised, and unconditionally append `FloorDivModule` instead of gating on opset>=9.
- Add `test_eq` covering ONNX `Equal` for opset>=11 (float equality was added after opset 11).
- Extend `test_remainder` / `test_remainder_scalar` with negative inputs across int64, float, and int32 dtypes, and with an integer scalar divisor, to validate the new integer `Mod` path.

Why: Integer floor division previously either raised at export time (opset7) or produced wrong results for negative operands (opset9 used `Floor(Div)`, which rounds toward zero for the `Div` op). PyTorch's `//` and `torch.remainder` must round toward negative infinity, so the exporter needs the `Mod`/`Where`-based correction and the opset11 `Mod` op to stay numerically correct.
messages.kimi:
[ONNX] Fix floor division and remainder for negative numbers and add eq op support

Fixes incorrect floor division results when inputs contain negative numbers by
correcting the rounding logic in _floor_divide to properly handle the fixup
calculation. Previously, the fixup subtraction was incorrectly applied based
on the division result rather than the condition mask.

Implements integer remainder support for ONNX opset 11+ using the Mod operator
with fmod_i=0, enabling proper remainder calculations for integer tensors.
For floating-point inputs, falls back to the existing floor division based
implementation.

Removes redundant floor division implementations from opset7 and opset8,
consolidating them into opset9 where the corrected logic resides. This
eliminates the opset version restriction that previously prevented FloorDiv
tests from running on older opset versions.

Adds missing equality operator test (test_eq) for ONNX export validation.

Adds comprehensive test coverage for remainder with negative numbers and
various dtypes (int64, float32, float64), and updates floor division tests
to use range-based inputs that include negative values for better edge case
validation.

Also fixed the fixup mask calculation in `_floor_divide` where negative division results were incorrectly adjusted. Added `remainder` implementation for opset 11 and added test coverage for negative number floor division and remainder cases.

[ONNX] Fix handling of uninitialized sequence outputs in control flow

Extend InferShapeTypeForUninitializedOutput to handle ListType (sequences)
in addition to TensorType. Previously, the ONNX exporter only handled
uninitialized tensor outputs in If subblocks, causing failures when
lists/sequences were returned from conditional branches. For ListType,
create a SequenceEmpty node with proper dtype attribute instead of a
Constant node. This enables proper ONNX export of models with list
operations in conditional branches, supported for ONNX opset >= 14.
messages.claude:
fix(onnx): support uninitialized ListType output in controlflow fixup

What:
- Extend `InferShapeTypeForUninitializedOutput` in `fixup_onnx_controlflow.cpp` to handle `ListType` outputs in addition to `TensorType`. When the sibling block output is a `ListType`, emit an `onnx::SequenceEmpty` node (with the inferred element dtype) instead of an `onnx::Constant` of zeros.
- Thread `opset_version` through `ONNXFixupUninitializedOutput` and `InferShapeTypeForUninitializedOutput`, then run `ONNXShapeTypeInference` on the newly created node so its type is populated correctly.
- Add five new ORT-backed tests (`test_uninitialized_tensorList`, `test_uninitialized_tensorList_dynamic`, `test_uninitialized_intList`, `test_uninitialized_tensorList_shape`, `test_sequance_loopcarried`) exercising uninitialized tensor/int list outputs and sequence loop-carried deps.
- Normalize comments: `onnx::identity` -> `onnx::Identity`.

Why:
Previously, when an `onnx::If` branch returned an uninitialized value while the other branch returned a sequence (`ListType`), the fixup pass assumed a `TensorType` and unconditionally built a tensor `Constant`. This crashed/fed the wrong type to downstream ops because a sequence output cannot be represented by a tensor zero constant. The exporter needs to materialize an empty `SequenceEmpty` (with proper element dtype) for such list-typed uninitialized outputs, and run shape/type inference so the ONNX graph is well-formed for ORT. The new tests guard both the tensor-list and int-list variants and the sequence loop-carried case, which require opset >= 13/14 due to ONNX `Identity` of sequence support.

messages.kimi:
feat: [ONNX] Support softplus with beta parameter in ONNX export

The softplus symbolic function previously only supported beta=1 and would fail with an unimplemented error for other beta values. This change extends the implementation to handle arbitrary beta values by computing softplus with beta as `Softplus(x * beta) / beta`, which is mathematically equivalent to the PyTorch softplus definition.

This enables exporting PyTorch models that use `torch.nn.functional.softplus` with non-default beta parameters to ONNX format.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] Support softplus with non-unit beta

Previously, the softplus symbolic converter in opset9 rejected any beta value other than 1 with an "unimplemented" error, limiting export coverage for models using torch.nn.functional.softplus with custom beta.

This change uses sym_help._maybe_get_const to extract the beta value at export time. For beta != 1, it emits the equivalent ONNX graph Softplus(Mul(x, beta)) / beta, matching the mathematical definition softplus(beta * x) / beta. For beta == 1, the original direct Softplus mapping is preserved.

Adds test coverage for beta=1, beta=2 (integer), and beta=1.7 (float) in test_pytorch_onnx_onnxruntime.py to validate the converter across constant types.
messages.minimax:
[ONNX] Support beta parameter in softplus export

Previously, `torch.nn.functional.softplus` with a beta parameter other than 1 was not supported during ONNX export and would raise an "unimplemented" error. This change implements proper beta support by applying the mathematical transformation: Softplus(x, beta) = Div(Softplus(Mul(x, beta)), beta). Tests are added to verify correct export with default beta, integer beta=2, and float beta=1.7.

Fixes the limitation where softplus with custom beta values could not be exported to ONNX.

[export] Integrate meta kernel generation with draft-export (#150809)

If a custom operator does not contain a fake impl, currently draft-export will use the real-tensor propagation to get an output for the operator and continue tracing. However if we retrace the exported model using `ep.run_decompositions`, or `export`, or run the exported program with fake tensors, we'll still fail because there's no fake impl.

With this PR, after draft-export we will generate an operator profile for each operator call that we encounter, and store this on the report attached to the exported program `ep._report.op_profiles`. Users can then use `torch._library.fake_profile.register_fake_profile` to temporarily generate and register a fake impl based on these operator profiles. This way future fake tensor retracing will work.

The workflow would look something like:
```python
class M(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, a, b):
        res = torch.ops.mylib.foo8(a, b)  # no fake impl
        return res

ep = export(M(), (torch.ones(3, 4), torch.ones(3, 4)) # this fails bc no fake impl
ep = draft_export(M(), (torch.ones(3, 4), torch.ones(3, 4))

ep.run_decompositions()  # this fails bc no fake impl
# this registers fake impls based on the profiles
with torch._library.fake_profile.register_fake_profile(ep._report.op_profiles):
    decomp = ep.run_decompositions()  # this works

new_inp = (
    torch.ones(2, 3, 4),
    torch.ones(2, 3, 4),
)
```

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/150809
Approved by: https://github.com/zou3519

messages.claude:
fix(datapipes): prevent in-place modification by deepcopying in IterableWrapper and removing redundant deepcopy in Mapper

What:
- Move the deepcopy responsibility from `Mapper._apply_fn` into `IterableWrapperIterDataPipe`, which now deepcopies its input iterable per iteration by default (configurable via `deepcopy` arg) and warns when deepcopy fails.
- Update the datapipe README to document the in-place modification pitfall and point to `IterableWrapper` as the reference for deepcopying.
- Replace the custom `IDP` test helper with `dp.iter.IterableWrapper` across `test/test_datapipe.py`, and harden the local `IDP_NoLen`-style stubs with `copy.deepcopy` to prevent in-place modification.
- Add `test_map_with_col_file_handle_datapipe` covering `map` with `input_col=1` over file-handle tuples/lists.
- Rename a few shadowing `dp` locals (`dp`/`it`) to `dp0`/`dp1`/`dp3`/`dp0`/`dp2` for clarity.

Why:
- Previously `Mapper` unconditionally deepcopied data when `input_col` was set, which is wasteful for non-mutable inputs and duplicates work that the source datapipe is better positioned to own. The in-place modification hazard actually lives at the source: when an `IterDataPipe` holds data in memory, a second iterator observes whatever the first iteration mutated. Centralizing the deepcopy in `IterableWrapper` (the typical source of in-memory data) ensures all downstream operations (Mapper, Filter, Collator, etc.) are protected uniformly and only pay the copy cost once at the source.
- Falling back to a warning (instead of raising) on non-deepcopyable inputs preserves backward compatibility and lets users opt into the old behavior via `deepcopy=False`, while still surfacing the risk of cross-iteration data inconsistency.
- Removing the bespoke `IDP`/`IDP_NoLen` test stubs in favor of the real `IterableWrapper` exercises the actual production code path and keeps test fixtures aligned with the new deepcopy contract; the deepcopy guard in the remaining local stubs prevents flaky cross-iteration failures.

2. Updates `Mapper._apply_fn` to remove the redundant `deepcopy` call since `IterableWrapper` now handles it upstream.

3. Updates all tests to use `IterableWrapper` instead of a custom `IDP` helper class, and adds a test verifying `map` with `input_col` and file handle datapipes works correctly with the new design.

messages.kimi:
feat: Support dim and keepdim arguments for torch.any and torch.all in ONNX export

Add support for `dim` and `keepdim` parameters in ONNX symbolic functions for `torch.any` and `torch.all`. Previously, these operations only supported reducing over all dimensions. The `_any` function now handles both `aten::any(Tensor self)` and `aten::any(Tensor self, int dim, bool keepdim)` signatures, passing the dimension and keepdim parameters to the ReduceSum operation. The `_all` function is updated to forward these arguments correctly to `_any` after applying the Not operation.

This enables users to export PyTorch models that use `x.any(dim=...)` or `x.all(dim=..., keepdim=...)` to ONNX format without encountering export errors or incorrect behavior.
messages.claude:
feat: support dim and keepdim args in ONNX any/all ops

Previously, the ONNX symbolic helpers for aten::any and aten::all only
supported the single-argument form (reduction over all elements), which
meant any calls passing `dim` or `keepdim` could not be exported to ONNX.

Update `_any` and `_all` in symbolic_opset9.py to accept the variadic
signature matching the two aten overloads:
- aten::any(Tensor self) / aten::all(Tensor self)
- aten::any(Tensor self, int dim, bool keepdim) / aten::all(...)

For the dim/keepdim variant, the reduction axes and keepdim flag are
forwarded to `_reducesum_helper` so the resulting ONNX ReduceSum has the

messages.kimi:
docs: Correct broadcasting documentation for 0-dim and empty tensors

Update the broadcasting rules documentation to accurately reflect PyTorch's actual behavior. The previous documentation incorrectly stated that tensors must have at least one dimension to be broadcastable, when in fact 0-dimensional tensors (scalars) are valid and broadcastable. Also clarify that empty tensors with shape (0,) are not automatically broadcastable due to trailing dimension mismatch. This aligns the documentation with the actual implementation and prevents user confusion when working with edge cases in tensor operations.
messages.claude:
docs: clarify broadcasting rules for zero-dimensional tensors

Update the broadcasting documentation to reflect that tensors no longer need at least one dimension to be broadcastable. The previous "at least one dimension" rule was removed because PyTorch now supports broadcasting of zero-dimensional (scalar) tensors against higher-dimensional tensors — a tensor with shape () is broadcastable since its shape "does not exist" along any given axis.

Also correct the illustrative examples to match the new semantics:
- Replace the 0-d tensor example from `torch.empty((0,))` (which is a 1-D tensor of length 0) with `torch.empty(())` (a true scalar), which now broadcasts successfully against a 2-D tensor.
- Add a new example showing that two non-trivial tensors whose trailing dimensions mismatch (e.g., 0 vs 2) remain non-broadcastable, ensuring the documented failure case still illustrates a genuine broadcast rule violation rather than the now-removed "at least one dimension" constraint.

This keeps the docs consistent with the actual broadcasting behavior implemented in `_broadcast_shapes`, so users are not misled into thinking scalar tensors cannot participate in broadcasting.

Simplify the broadcasting documentation by removing the redundant "at least one dimension" rule and add clearer examples showing:

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix sampler reproducibility when generator is None

When generator=None, RandomSampler was assigning a new generator to
self.generator with a random seed, causing the sampler to produce
different sequences across multiple iterations of the same instance.
This broke reproducibility expectations.

Changes:
- Use local generator variable instead of modifying self.generator
- Ensure fresh random seed for each __iter__ call when generator=None
- Consistently use yield/yield from in all samplers for proper
  iterator behavior
- Add comprehensive tests for sampler reproducibility

This ensures that multiple iterations over the same sampler instance
produce consistent, reproducible results when manually seeded.
messages.claude:
fix: make samplers reproducible across iterations

RandomSampler previously cached its generator as an instance attribute on the first call to __iter__. The generator's RNG state advanced after consuming randperm/randint, so a second iteration of the same sampler instance would resume from the mutated state instead of reproducing the original sequence. This broke reproducibility when a sampler was iterated more than once (e.g., across epochs or when combining list(sampler) + list(sampler)).

The fix stops storing the lazily-created generator on self: a local generator is built from a fresh seed each time __iter__ is entered, while an explicitly-provided self.generator is still honored. This makes every iteration of a given sampler deterministic and independent of prior iteration history.

Additionally, SubsetRandomSampler and WeightedRandomSampler were converted from returning a generator expression / iter() over a materialized list to using yield-based generators. This aligns them with RandomSampler's iteration model and is required for the reproducibility semantics above, since a returned iterator constructed lazily over the generator would otherwise hold onto and mutate shared RNG state in surprising ways.

Tests in test/test_dataloader.py::test_sampler_reproducibility are extended to cover the new contract: each sampler type (RandomSampler with/without replacement, WeightedRandomSampler with/without replacement, SubsetRandomSampler) is iterated twice under the same torch.manual_seed and asserted to produce identical sequences, both via repeated list(sampler) calls and via two independent iterators advanced in lockstep.
messages.minimax:
fix: improve sampler reproducibility and generator handling

The samplers had issues where iterating multiple times over the same sampler would not produce reproducible results even when the generator was seeded identically. This was caused by:

- `RandomSampler`: The generator was unconditionally used and updated in-place, causing state to diverge on subsequent iterations
- `SubsetRandomSampler`: Used a generator expression which doesn't properly interface with external generators
- `WeightedRandomSampler`: Used `return iter(...)` instead of `yield from`, preventing proper generator behavior

The fix restructures `RandomSampler.__iter__` to create a local generator reference (new or existing), and converts `SubsetRandomSampler` and `WeightedRandomSampler` to use explicit `yield from` syntax, matching the pattern used by `RandomSampler`.

feat: support tuple outputs in lazy tensor codegen

Add multi-output (tuple) support to the lazy tensor codegen pipeline so
operators like native_layer_norm, native_layer_norm_backward, and topk can
be lowered correctly.

Why:
- Previously compute_shape_* / compute_dtype_* returned a single shape
  and dtype, which only worked for single-output ops. Tuple-output ops
  either had to be hand-written or were incorrectly codegen'd.
- This change makes Node carry plural at_dtypes_/at_shapes_, updates the
  codegen to emit std::vector-based shape/dtype APIs, and threads
  multiple outputs through CreateFrom via a new
  TupleAtenFromLtcTensors helper.
- Also fixes optional operand handling in Node construction and TS
  lowering so optional tensor inputs (e.g. weight/bias in layer_norm)
  are skipped rather than hashed as kNullValue, which was incorrect
  for multi-operand nodes.
- Adds bool ListCType support in the lazy codegen to handle
  output_mask arguments (e.g. native_layer_norm_backward).

The code changes reshape the meta-function signatures
(compute_shape_* returns vector<vector<int64_t>>,
compute_dtype_* returns vector<c10::ScalarType>), add the corresponding
Node constructor, and update the codegen templates to emit multi-output
bridge calls.
messages.kimi:
feat: Add support for tuple outputs in Lazy Tensor Core IR

This change adds infrastructure to support operators with tuple outputs in the Lazy Tensor Core (LTC) IR system. The modifications include:

1. IR Node Enhancement: Extended `Node` class to store ATEN dtypes and shapes as vectors, enabling representation of multiple outputs per operation. Added a new constructor accepting `at_dtypes` and `at_shapes` parameters.

2. Shape/Dtype Computation: Updated `compute_shape_*` and `compute_dtype_*` functions to return `std::vector<std::vector<int64_t>>` and `std::vector<c10::ScalarType>` respectively, supporting multi-output operations like `native_layer_norm` and `native_layer_norm_backward`.

3. Code Generation Updates: Modified lazy tensor code generators to handle tuple outputs, including proper bridge conversion using `TupleAtenFromLtcTensors` template.

4. New Operations: Added `native_layer_norm`, `native_layer_norm_backward`, and `topk` to the full codegen list in `ts_native_functions.yaml`.

5. Utility Functions: Added helper templates `CreateComputationShapeFromMetaTensors` and `CreateDTypeFromMetaTensors` for extracting shape and dtype information from tuple outputs.

This enables LTC to properly handle operations that return multiple tensors, which is essential for complete PyTorch operator coverage.

messages.kimi:
feat: Support ONNX_FALLTHROUGH for autograd functions

When exporting models with custom autograd functions using `OperatorExportTypes.ONNX_FALLTHROUGH`, the export fails with "Couldn't export Python operator" error. This happens because the validation logic in `export.cpp` unconditionally rejects `prim::PythonOp` nodes regardless of the `ONNX_FALLTHROUGH` export type.

This change modifies the validation logic to skip the Python operator export error when `ONNX_FALLTHROUGH` is enabled, allowing autograd functions to pass through as `prim::PythonOp` nodes. This aligns with the expected behavior of ONNX_FALLTHROUGH mode, which should allow unsupported operators to be preserved in the graph rather than failing export.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] allow fallthrough export of Python autograd operators

When exporting a graph containing a prim::PythonOp (e.g. a custom
torch.autograd.Function), the exporter unconditionally raised a
FAIL_EXPORT error. This made it impossible to use the
ONNX_FALLTHROUGH operator_export_type to inspect such graphs, since
the validation in validateBlock rejected Python ops before the
fallthrough path had a chance to emit them verbatim.

Skip the Python-op error when operator_export_type is
ONNX_FALLTHROUGH so the node is preserved as prim::PythonOp in the
exported graph, mirroring the existing behavior for other unsupported
operators under fallthrough mode. Adds test_autograd_onnx_fallthrough
to cover a custom autograd.Function exported with ONNX_FALLTHROUGH.

What

feat: Add code-generated add.Tensor and improve wrapped number handling

Add support for code-generating the add.Tensor operation in the lazy tensor backend. Introduce GetLtcTensorOrCreateForWrappedNumber() helper to properly handle scalar tensors (wrapped numbers) by creating lazy tensors when needed. Add variadic GetLtcDevice() template for multi-tensor device inference. Remove hand-written add implementations from tensor_aten_ops and aten_ltc_ts_type to use the code-generated versions instead. Update lazy_ir.py to use consistent lazy_ prefix for tensor variables and handle wrapped numbers in lazy tensor declarations.
messages.claude:
fix: handle wrapped number tensors and use variadic GetLtcDevice in lazy IR codegen

What:
- Add bridge::GetLtcTensorOrCreateForWrappedNumber to create an LTC tensor
  for 0-dim wrapped number tensors instead of treating them as regular
  tensors.
- Add a variadic template overload of GetLtcDevice that walks a pack of
  tensors and returns the first non-nullopt device.
- Update lazy_ir.py codegen to:
  - Emit the variadic GetLtcDevice call for all value-type inputs.
  - Rename generated locals from l_<name> to lazy_<name>.
  - Use GetLtcTensorOrCreateForWrappedNumber for BaseCType value tensors.
- Remove the handwritten LazyNativeFunctions::add and its tensor_aten_ops
  helpers so add.Tensor falls back to the codegen path.
- Drop the stale bitwise_and.Scalar full_codegen entry.

Why:
Wrapped number tensors (e.g. scalar Python numbers lifted to 0-dim CPU
tensors) were not being converted to lazy tensors, so ops like
add.Tensor produced incorrect results or crashed when a wrapped number
was passed as an argument. Routing them through
GetLtcTensorOrCreateForWrappedNumber ensures they participate in lazy
lowering. Moving add.Tensor out of the supported/handwritten path and
into codegen (with the device inferred via the variadic GetLtcDevice)
removes the divergence between handwritten and generated ops and fixes
the underlying correctness bug. The bitwise_and.Scalar entry is removed
because that op is not actually supported by the TS backend.
messages.minimax:
refactor(lazy_tensor_core): use codegen for add.Tensor and fix device resolution for wrapped numbers

The add operation was previously implemented manually but is now routed through codegen. This required:

1. Adding GetLtcTensorOrCreateForWrappedNumber to handle Python-wrapped number tensors which need special device resolution via GetOrCreateLtcTensor instead of GetLtcTensor.
2. Adding a variadic GetLtcDevice template to resolve the device from multiple value tensors, enabling correct device lookup in codegen'd ops.
3. Updating lazy_ir.py to use lazy_ prefix for tensor variable names and inject device resolution at the start of generated functions.
4. Moving add.Tensor from full_codegen to supported in ts_native_functions.yaml since it now uses the codegen path with the new bridge helpers.

This unifies the add implementation with other tensor operations and fixes device resolution for wrapped number handling.

Make torch._chunk_cat support non-contiguous inputs (#151263)

Currently, `torch._chunk_cat` only supports contiguous inputs (due to `.view()` usage in `_pad_chunk()` supporting only contiguous tensor). This doesn't work for internal models where there can be non-contiguous input tensors:

- size=[8192, 16416], stride=[16448, 1]  # stride[0] is larger than size[1]
- size=[1152, 384], stride=[1, 1152]  # column-major tensor

In this PR, we relax the assumption on contiguous input tensor, by switching from `.view()` to `.reshape()`. Note that since `.reshape()` will try to use `.view()` under the hood whenever possible, this should not cause regression to existing use cases.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add full codegen support for relu, relu_, and zero_ ops in lazy tensor core

This commit migrates the relu, relu_, and zero_ operations from manual implementations to full code-generated implementations in the lazy tensor core backend. The changes include:

1. Moving relu, relu_, and zero_ from the "supported" list to "full_codegen" in ts_native_functions.yaml, enabling automatic generation of IR classes, shape inference, and lowering logic.

2. Adding compute_shape_relu, compute_dtype_relu, compute_shape_zero, and compute_dtype_zero functions to LazyShapeDtype.cpp to support shape and dtype inference for these operations.

3. Removing manual implementations of ReluOp, relu, relu_, and zero_ from ops.cpp, ops.h, tensor_aten_ops.cpp, tensor_aten_ops.h, and aten_ltc_ts_type.cpp, as they are now auto-generated.

4. Refactoring the code generation infrastructure in lazy_ir.py to properly handle in-place variants by introducing GenLazyNativeFuncDefinition class and ComputeShapeSignature class, ensuring shape inference functions use base names to avoid duplication between functional and in-place variants.

5. Adding sorting of native functions in gen_lazy_tensor.py to ensure consistent code generation order and prevent edge cases where in-place variants might be processed before their functional counterparts.

The motivation is to reduce manual boilerplate code, improve maintainability, and ensure consistent behavior across the lazy tensor core backend by leveraging the code generation infrastructure for these common activation and initialization operations.
messages.claude:
refactor: move relu and zero_ ops to codegen path and unify in-place variant handling

Summary:
- Removed hand-written implementations of `relu`, `relu_`, and `zero_` across the lazy_tensor_core backend (ops.cpp/h, tensor_aten_ops.cpp/h, aten_ltc_ts_type.cpp, ts_node_lowering.cpp) and instead listed them under `full_codegen` in ts_native_functions.yaml.
- Added `compute_shape_relu`/`compute_dtype_relu` and `compute_shape_zero`/`compute_dtype_zero` meta functions in LazyShapeDtype.cpp so the codegen can derive output shape/dtype.
- Introduced `LazyIrSchema.base_name` in tools/codegen/api/lazy.py to express the base (non-variant) name of an op, used to share shape/dtype compute signatures between functional and in-place variants.
- Converted `gen_lazy_nativefunc_definition` into the `GenLazyNativeFuncDefinition` dataclass and extracted a `ComputeShapeSignature` helper so shape/dtype decls and calls consistently use the base name, avoiding duplicate/missing symbols for in-place variants.
- Extended `concat_map_codegen` with a `codegenInplaceVariant` flag and a `generated` set, and sorted `grouped_native_functions` by function name, so that in-place variants reuse the IR class generated for their functional counterpart without emitting duplicate or mis-attributed nodes.

Why:
The codegen pipeline previously had no way to handle functional and in-place variants of the same op together: `relu`/`relu_` and `zero_` were hand-rolled to work around this. When these ops were moved into `full_codegen`, naively emitting shape/dtype functions keyed on the full aten name (e.g. `compute_shape_relu_`) produced symbols that didn't match the in-place call sites, and emitting an IR node for `relu_` before `relu` would attribute `at::aten::relu_` to the shared IR class, breaking `relu`. The base-name abstraction, the in-place codegen flag, and the deterministic sort together let functional and in-place variants share IR classes, lowerings, and shape inference while emitting a single canonical set of symbols, eliminating the hand-written special cases and unblocking the migration of more ops onto the codegen path.
messages.minimax:
Move relu/relu_/zero_ to full codegen with proper inplace variant handling

The lazy tensor codebase had hand-written implementations for relu, relu_, and zero_ that used SetShapeDeferred with dynamic_pointer_cast, which is both inefficient and inconsistent with other ops. This commit moves these ops to full codegen and fixes the codegen to properly handle inplace variants by using the base op name (relu instead of relu_) when generating IR classes, shape functions, and dtype functions. Also fixes namespace formatting and a typo.

The change adds two new overloads in `aten_ltc_ts_type.cpp` (random_.from and random_.to) and updates the Random node class to store and lower these optional bounds. The ts_native_functions.yaml is updated to register the new supported operations. Test tolerance is also relaxed from 0.15 to 0.2 to accommodate the increased variance in bounded random generation across different dtypes.
messages.claude:
feat: support from/to overloads for aten::random_ in lazy tensor core

Previously only the no-argument form of aten::random_ was implemented for
the lazy tensor backend. This adds the from and to overloads (registered
in ts_native_functions.yaml as random_.from and random_.to) and threads
the optional from/to bounds through the Random IR node, its ToString,
and its Lower path so the bounds are correctly forwarded to the
lowered builtin.

Why: aten::random_ exposes three overloads (default, from-only, and
from/to), but only the default overload was wired up. Calling the
bounded variants on a lazy tensor would either fall back to eager or
produce incorrect results because the bounds were silently dropped.
This makes all three overloads first-class lazy citizens and preserves
generator-defined behavior by routing to the fallback when a generator
is supplied.

Also bumps the tolerance in TestRandomInPlace from 0.15 to 0.2 to keep
the probabilistic test stable across the newly exercised code paths.
messages.minimax:
feat: Add from/to range support to random_ tensor operation

Extend the `aten::random_` operation to support optional `from` and `to` range parameters, enabling random tensor generation within a specified integer range.

- Add `from` and `to` c10::optional<int64_t> members to the Random IR node
- Implement Random::ToString() for debugging and Random::Lower() for TorchScript lowering
- Add three overloads of random_ in LazyNativeFunctions to handle: (from, to), (to), and no-args cases
- Register random_.from and random_.to in ts_native_functions.yaml
- Adjust test epsilon from 0.15 to 0.2 in TestRandomInPlaceDefaultFrom to account for new range semantics

Make torch._chunk_cat support non-contiguous inputs (#151263)

Currently, `torch._chunk_cat` only supports contiguous inputs (due to `.view()` usage in `_pad_chunk()` supporting only contiguous tensor). This doesn't work for internal models where there can be non-contiguous input tensors:

- size=[8192, 16416], stride=[16448, 1]  # stride[0] is larger than size[1]
- size=[1152, 384], stride=[1, 1152]  # column-major tensor

In this PR, we relax the assumption on contiguous input tensor, by switching from `.view()` to `.reshape()`. Note that since `.reshape()` will try to use `.view()` under the hood whenever possible, this should not cause regression to existing use cases.

Refactor index_select to use full codegen instead of manual IR lowering

Previously index_select used a custom IndexSelect IR node with manual lowering logic in ts_node_lowering.cpp. This required maintaining separate shape/dtype computation, tensor_aten_ops wrapping, and TS lowering code.

This change moves index_select to full_codegen in ts_native_functions.yaml, enabling automatic code generation to handle these concerns. The custom IndexSelect IR node, its Infer/Lower implementations, and the manual tensor_aten_ops::index_select wrapper are all removed.

The test is also enhanced to verify negative dimension indices work correctly (testing with offset -2 in addition to 0).
messages.kimi:
refactor: Migrate index_select to full_codegen and improve dimension handling

Migrate the index_select operation from manual C++ implementation to the
auto-generated full_codegen system. This eliminates boilerplate code in
favor of code generation, improving maintainability and consistency with
other operations.

The migration requires adding compute_shape_index_select and
compute_dtype_index_select functions to LazyShapeDtype.cpp to provide
shape and dtype inference for the generated code. These functions follow
the PyTorch documentation semantics for index_select, including proper
handling of rank-0 index tensors by promoting them to 1x1.

Also fix compute_shape_cat to use at::maybe_wrap_dim instead of manual
dimension canonicalization, ensuring consistent dimension handling across
the codebase. Add test coverage for negative dimension indices in
index_select to verify correct behavior with wrapped dimensions.
messages.claude:
refactor: move index_select to codegen and replace manual dim wrapping with at::maybe_wrap_dim

Move index_select from manual IR op implementation (IndexSelect class, LowerIndexSelect, InferIndexSelect) to the codegen pipeline by adding it to ts_native_functions.yaml's full_codegen list. This removes ~60 lines of hand-maintained lowering/shape-inference code in favor of the generated path, consistent with how other similar ops (e.g. kl_div_backward) are handled.

Also fix two correctness issues uncovered along the way:
- index_select now handles rank-0 index tensors by promoting them to 1*1, matching PyTorch's documented semantics (compute_shape_index_select).
- compute_shape_cat previously hand-rolled dim normalization (dim % rank; canonical_dim += rank) which diverged from PyTorch's canonical behavior for negative dims. Switch it to at::maybe_wrap_dim(dim, tensors) so cat accepts the same negative dim values as eager.

Tests extended to cover negative dim offsets for index_select (looping over {-2, 0}).

Why: the hand-written lowering duplicated logic already provided by codegen + at::maybe_wrap_dim, and the bespoke dim wrapping in cat was inconsistent with eager, causing negative-dim inputs to be mishandled. Consolidating onto the shared helpers reduces maintenance surface and fixes the divergence.

messages.claude:
[ONNX] Fold constant input for Gather with rank > 1 indices

The previous constant folding implementation for ONNX::Gather returned
`c10::nullopt` whenever the indices tensor had rank > 1, which caused
constant folding to be skipped for Gather ops with multi-dimensional
constant indices. This is a common pattern in transformer models where
`torch.nn.Embedding` (which lowers to ONNX::Gather) is fed constant mask
inputs.

The root cause was an ordering issue: the rank check was performed
*after* calling `at::index_select`, which only supports indices with
rank <= 1 (see https://pytorch.org/docs/master/generated/torch.index_select.html).
This meant the unsupported path was entered before the guard could
short-circuit, so the fold never succeeded for rank > 1 inputs and the
error path was unreachable in practice.

This change moves the rank check ahead of the `at::index_select` call so
that high-rank constant indices cause an early `nullopt` return (skipping
fold cleanly) rather than invoking an unsupported aten op. The test for
`GatherModule` is extended to include a constant-fed `torch.nn.Embedding`
so the folding path is exercised end-to-end via ONNX Runtime.

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/156023
Approved by: https://github.com/Skylion007
messages.minimax:

Move the rank check for indices (q > 1) before the negative index adjustment logic in runTorchBackendForOnnx. Previously, indices were manipulated (adjusting for negative values) before checking if rank exceeded 1, causing unnecessary computation. Now the early return for multi-dimensional indices happens first, avoiding wasteful operations. Also add a test case using torch.nn.Embedding which is converted to ONNX::Gather — a common pattern for constant mask inputs in transformer models.
messages.kimi:
[ONNX] Fix constant folding for Gather with high-rank indices

Move the rank check for indices before calling at::index_select in the ONNX constant folding pass for Gather operations. The at::index_select operator only supports indices with rank <= 1, so we need to validate this and return early to avoid potential errors when processing Gather nodes with high-rank index inputs.

This pattern is common for constant mask inputs in transformer models where torch.nn.Embedding is converted to ONNX::Gather.

feat: Add ONNX export support for torch.addcmul operator

Implement symbolic function for `torch.addcmul` in ONNX opset9 to enable exporting models using this operation. The function decomposes addcmul into the ONNX equivalent: `self + (tensor1 * tensor2 * value)`, supporting both default value=1.0 and custom scalar multiplier.

This extends PyTorch's ONNX export coverage for element-wise tensor operations, allowing users to export models that use addcmul for fused multiply-add computations with an optional scaling factor.
messages.claude:
[ONNX] Add symbolic for addcmul

Implement ONNX symbolic support for torch.addcmul, which computes
self + value * tensor1 * tensor2. The operator is decomposed into
existing ONNX ops: mul(tensor1, tensor2) scaled by a constant value,
then added to self. This unblocks exporting models that rely on
addcmul (e.g. certain optimizer update and attention path patterns)
to ONNX without falling back to ATen.

A corresponding onnxruntime round-trip test is added covering both
the default value=1.0 and a custom value, plus broadcasted input
shapes, to guard against regressions in the decomposition.

```py
import torch

model = BfloatModel()
onnx_program = torch.onnx.export(model, (input,), dynamo=True, optimize=False, verify=True)
```

feat: Add ONNX symbolic support for torch.nan_to_num, torch.maximum, and torch.minimum

Add symbolic conversion for `torch.nan_to_num` in opset 10 using IsNaN, IsInf, and Where ops to replace NaN and infinite values with specified finite values. Add `torch.maximum` and `torch.minimum` aliases in opset 9 that delegate to existing min/max symbolic functions. Introduce `pytorch_name_to_type` mapping in symbolic_helper.py to enable dtype-aware tensor construction during conversion. messages.claude:
[ONNX] Add symbolic export for nan_to_num, maximum, and minimum ops

Implement ONNX symbolic functions for torch.nan_to_num in opset10 and torch.maximum/minimum in opset9. Previously these ops lacked exporters, causing ONNX export of models using them to fail.

- nan_to_num: handles None values for nan/posinf/neginf by defaulting to 0.0 and the dtype's finite min/max (via torch.finfo). Non-floating-point inputs are returned as-is since int tensors cannot represent inf/nan. Uses IsNaN/IsInf + Where to map values, requiring opset 10 (IsInf is introduced in opset 10).
- maximum/minimum: delegate to the existing max/min symbolic with dim_or_y, exposing the elementwise variants currently routed through the dim reduction path.
- Add pytorch_name_to_type mapping in symbolic_helper to resolve scalar type names (e.g. "Float") to torch dtypes, needed to construct correctly-typed replacement constants.
- Add opset-gated tests covering nan_to_num with/without params across float/half/int inputs, and maximum/minimum with NaN inputs.
